text:
Mia Chen: @channel quick triage - Cypher LoRA merge produced unexpected token alignment diffs after int4 quant. Quickpack attached, need a fast decision before we push to Dedicated. :eyes:

Sam Patel: can you drop the eval summary and artifact links? quick numbers will help.

Mia Chen: pasted quick summary:
```
Model: redwood/cypher-base + cypher-lora-v2
Config: quant=int4, qscheme=4bit-ptq
Quickpack: 2024-11-03
Metrics: ppl: base 12.3 -> merged 13.7 (+11%), exact_match: 0.82 -> 0.76 (-6 points)
Failure modes: token alignment in code fences, tokenized IDs shifted for `|` char
Artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/cypher/quickpack-236501
```

Asha Rao: :grimacing: token ID shift sounds like a tokenizer/vocab mismatch. Did the finetune add special tokens? LoRA normally shouldn't.

Sam Patel: the finetune included a tiny vocab patch to handle Cypher doc markers. Merge process pulled that in. Commands used for reproducibility:
```
scripts/merge_lora.py --base redwood/cypher-base --lora cypher-lora-v2 --out merged/cypher-lora-merged
python quantize.py --model merged/cypher-lora-merged --q int4 --out merged/cypher-lora-merged-int4
```

Ryan Gomez: if vocab changed, the quantizer/tokenizer boundary can remap token ids. Quick check: compare tokenizer.encode("`|`") before/after.

Sam Patel: ran that locally, output:
```
# before
tokenizer.encode("`|`") -> [987, 45]
# after
tokenizer.encode("`|`") -> [1012]  # single token, shifted
```

Asha Rao: that explains the alignment break in code fences. Two remediation paths: 1) re-export the merged model with the original tokenizer (remove vocab patch), or 2) implement an id-remap shim at quantize/export to preserve original token ids. Option 2 is lower surface risk for behavior.

Mia Chen: Cypher is strict about no behavioral diffs. Prefer id remap. How invasive is it?

Sam Patel: I can add a remap table during quantize/export. Minimal change. Example pattern:
```
# remap_ids.json
{"1012": [987,45], "1015": [300]}  # example map where new single token maps back to old ids
quantize.py --remap remap_ids.json --model merged/... --out merged/...-remap
```

Eval Bot: quickpack run finished for remap build: merged-int4+remap -> ppl 12.6, exact_match 0.81, code-block alignment fixed on 98% of sampled examples. Full artifact: s3://redwood-evals/cypher/quickpack-236501-remap

Asha Rao: good. Let's add a deterministic unit in the smoke pack asserting tokenizer.encode for top special tokens remains identical pre/post. Also add a small fuzz test for code fence sequences.

Ryan Gomez: agreed. Rollout suggestion: canary 5% on Dedicated-cypher with automatic fallback to base if error >1% or regression in exact_match >2 points over 30m. Add tracing hook to capture tokenization diffs for first 1k requests.

Mia Chen: I'll draft the rollout config and request SLO review. Owners: @Sam Patel, @Asha Rao. I'll kick off a full eval tonight and report back.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: group="dedicated-cypher-canary" image="merged/cypher-lora-merged-int4-remap" start=2024-11-04T02:00:00Z

Sam Patel: will run the full eval and push any fixes.

Mia Chen: thanks team, this remap path seems safest for Cypher. Follow-ups: add smoke unit, run full eval, schedule canary. :rocket:
